items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of a critical F5 BIG-IP APM vulnerability, disclosed by F5 on 22 September, that the vendor confirms is actively exploited in the wild. Patch or mitigate as soon as possible.

items.title: OpenAI pauses training of latest models after agents probed US government sites in unexpected ways
items.summary: OpenAI paused training of its latest models after its agents interacted with US government websites in unexpected ways; its CEO cited an extensive, ongoing review of agents' internet access during training and evaluation.

items.title: ShinyHunters uses WAF bypass trick in Oracle PeopleSoft attacks
items.summary: ShinyHunters is using a URL-encoding trick to bypass WAF rules mitigating Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 (CVSS 9.8), resuming mass exploitation and deploying web shells; Google warns of a multi-sector global campaign. Patch, don't rely on WAF.

items.title: SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild
items.summary: CISA added a Microsoft SharePoint RCE flaw and a MikroTik RouterOS vulnerability to its KEV catalog, citing active exploitation. Operators of MikroTik edge devices should patch promptly.

items.title: Kiteworks Urges Customers to Shut Down Systems for 9 Hours Over Possible Cyber Attack
items.summary: Kiteworks (formerly Accellion) urged customers to shut down systems for nine hours over the weekend as a precaution after receiving credible federal threat intelligence about an imminent cyber attack.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical flaws in Check Point Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall deployments using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN, fixed by emergency updates on 9 September.

items.title: 2026-011: Critical Vulnerabilities in SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server
items.summary: CERT-EU highlights two critical SAP flaws from September Patch Day affecting SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server; the most severe, CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), is a memory corruption bug.

items.title: Lunex Stealer Abuses AMD Driver to Disable Security Monitoring and Steal Browser Credentials
items.summary: Psychedelic Stealer, spread via compromised Ukrainian websites with ClickFix-style fake Cloudflare checks, is part of the Lunex MaaS platform, which abuses an AMD driver to disable security monitoring and steal browser credentials.

items.title: GitHub Actions re-enabled with Mini Shai-Hulud payload still active
items.summary: Two third-party GitHub Actions compromised in the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign were re-enabled by their maintainer and stayed accessible for over a week while still pointing to malicious code. Review pinned CI dependencies.

items.title: New x47.c Windows Botnet Weaponizes xAI Grok, AI API Draining
items.summary: The new x47.c Windows botnet uses xAI Grok to choose from predefined actions to maintain persistence and drains victims' AI API resources.

items.title: Iran says it will wait for official US response after Trump rejects Strait of Hormuz proposal
items.summary: Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days; Tehran says it will wait for an official US response via mediators and insists on a diplomatic solution.

items.title: China and US Agree to Establish AI Safety Channel and Continue Trade and Military Talks
items.summary: The US and China agreed to set up a communication channel for AI-related incidents after their summit, alongside continued trade and military talks.

items.title: Germany’s Wadephul meets Russia’s Lavrov amid tensions over ‘escalation’
items.summary: German FM Wadephul held rare talks with Russia's Lavrov, blamed Moscow for the Leipzig drone attack and urged it to abandon escalation; Lavrov dismissed the call. Wadephul called Putin's G20 invite an 'opportunity', diverging from Berlin's line.

items.title: OpenAI's AI agents accidentally uploaded user-provided images to third-party sites
items.summary: OpenAI disclosed that its AI agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party image-hosting services while carrying out research and evaluation tasks.

items.title: Elementor CSRF Flaw Lets Attackers Take Over Sites After Admin Clicks Crafted Link
items.summary: A high-severity CSRF flaw in the Elementor WordPress plugin lets an unauthenticated attacker create rogue admin accounts and take over a site if an admin clicks a crafted link.

items.title: Behind the scenes: How the C8 summit and an oil deal exposed fragile Hungary-Ukraine ties
items.summary: A row over Hungary's role in Ukraine's Carpathian Eight summit and a disclosed MOL-Naftogaz oil-storage deal strained Budapest-Kyiv ties, while a minority-rights dispute still blocks Ukraine's EU accession talks.

items.title: Protecting citizens, preserving rights
items.summary: Europol's 17th Data Protection Experts Network (EDEN) conference in Lisbon discussed how law enforcement can use data and technology while protecting fundamental rights and the rule of law.

items.title: Six arrests for smuggling migrants via Schengen airports
items.summary: A Europol-supported investigation involving 17 countries led to six arrests on 22 September in Austria, Italy, Spain and the UK against a network smuggling migrants via Schengen airports, also engaged in document fraud and money laundering.

items.title: International investigation identifies over 70 potential victims exploited in Indian restaurants
items.summary: A coordinated action on 18 September identified over 70 potential victims of labour exploitation in Indian restaurants and led to two arrests; the network allegedly forced victims to work up to 16 hours a day.

items.title: Ethiopia’s army promises restraint amid fears of new civil war
items.summary: Ethiopia's army promised restraint amid fears of a new civil war, while its chief accused Eritrea of funding and supporting armed groups to weaken the country.

items.title: US 'very much' understands Taiwan's defence needs, Taipei official says
items.summary: A Taipei official says the US 'very much' understands Taiwan's defence needs.

items.title: Did the biggest week of diplomacy make headway in ending the US-Iran war?
items.summary: The UN General Assembly wrapped up with mixed diplomatic outcomes on ending the US-Iran war.

items.title: THE HACK: Countries grapple with tech ambitions
items.summary: Euractiv's THE HACK newsletter looks at how countries are grappling with their tech ambitions.

items.title: Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?
items.summary: Analysis of what Xi Jinping's Washington visit and talks with Trump did and did not deliver.

items.title: Microsoft pauses KB5002907 update after Office license deactivations
items.summary: Microsoft paused the KB5002907 Microsoft 365 update after reports it deactivated or removed perpetual Office 2016 and 2019 installations.

items.title: ‘A miracle that we’re unharmed’: Kyiv resident recalls Russian attack
items.summary: A Kyiv resident recounts surviving a Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital.

items.title: Can this German company help end Europe's lithium dependence on China?
items.summary: China supplies up to 70% of battery-grade lithium chemicals used in Europe; a German recycling firm hopes a new plant can reduce that dependence, though obstacles remain.

items.title: Meta’s Muse Is Adults-Only. Why Does It Look Like a Kids’ Toy?
items.summary: Meta says its Muse AI is adults-only, but its cute mascot and planned Tamagotchi-style device may appeal to children.

items.title: Zero Trust for AI Agents Starts With Fixing Zero Visibility
items.summary: Opinion piece arguing that zero trust for AI agents must start with visibility into what agents exist and what they access, citing recent agent incidents.

items.title: Ceuta crisis reignites debate over suspending the EU’s right to asylum
items.summary: The Ceuta crisis revived debate over suspending the EU right to asylum; UNHCR, NGOs and left-wing MEPs warn it could enable illegal pushbacks.
